questions.solution:

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is an interrogative sentence. The answer to this question will be either "yes" or "no".

These types of sentences usually begin with a helping verb like: Do, does.

The format of such a sentence in Active voice is: Do/Does + Subject + V1 + Object?

Therefore, in Passive voice, the format will be: Am/Is/Are + Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)?

For example:

Does he need a therapy? (Active)

Is a therapy needed by him? (Passive)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Thus, the correct answer is option (b): Is the butter not licked by Sneha?

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: The decision to change a hospital saved an life of the daughter of the doctor.
options.html: The decision to change a hospital saved an life of the daughter of the doctor.

options.text: The decision to change the hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.
options.html: The decision to change the hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.

options.text: The decision to change an hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.
options.html: The decision to change an hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.

options.text: A decision to change a hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.
options.html: A decision to change a hospital saved the life of the daughter of the doctor.

questions.solution:
Option (a): It is grammatically incorrect because 'life' is a consonant-sounding word and hence cannot be preceded by the indefinite article 'an'.

Option (c): It is grammatically incorrect because 'hospital' is a consonant-sounding word and hence cannot be preceded by the indefinite article 'an'.

Option (d): It is grammatically incorrect as the sentence in question discusses the particular decision of changing the hospital. So, 'decision' should be preceded by the definite article 'the', and not 'a'.

Option (b) is grammatically correct.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

The moon is Earth's only natural satellite and the nearby large celestial body.
questions.solution:
'The nearby large' does not give any meaning to the sentence. It fails to imply that moon is a large celestial body around the Earth.

'The near largest' is incorrect as the adjective in positive degree does not require 'the' before it unless we imply the plural sense (as in the rich, the poor).

'The nearly large' is incorrect as 'nearly' (means 'closely') does not help make the sentence meaningful.

Option (b) is the correct replacement and implies that the satellite/celestial body nearest to Earth is 'moon'.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

These types of questions contain Modal verbs. Some of the modal verbs are: Can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, ought to.

The format of such a sentence in Active Voice is: Subject + Modal + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + Modal + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

You can do this. (Active Voice)
